issue.title: Specify D2 reproducibility semantics and Gate K confidence-bounded empirical claims protocol
issue.body:
This PR resolves the missing normative spec for behavioral graph equivalence vs byte reproducibility (PDF §15 / D2) and formalizes the statistical protocol required for empirical claims. It closes the gap called out in Plan §9.23 by turning placeholder language into a concrete, referenced specification.

- **Spec addition: BR vs BE + empirical protocol**
  - Added `docs/transformerless/EQUIVALENCE_AND_EMPIRICAL_PROTOCOL.md` as the normative source for:
    - **Class BR (byte reproducible)** for certificate-bearing artifacts (identical pinned inputs ⇒ identical bytes/CIDs).
    - **Class BE (behaviorally equivalent)** for non-canonical/platform-accelerated compiles using declared equivalence margins and confidence bounds.
    - Gate K claim requirements: mandatory claim record fields, estimator/CI requirements, and acceptance rules for threshold, equivalence, and non-inferiority claims.

- **D2 integration in wire-format RFC**
  - Updated `docs/transformerless/R4G1.md` §7 to reference the new normative spec and remove “working assumption” ambiguity.
  - Clarifies BR is required for Gate E artifacts; BE is permitted for local accelerated compiles under the protocol.

- **Plan §9.23 linkage**
  - Updated `docs/r4_graph_compiler_implementation_plan.md` backlog item 23 to point directly to the new spec document.

```markdown
- Lower-bounded claim (`metric >= t`): accepted iff CI lower bound `>= t`.
- Upper-bounded claim (`metric <= t`): accepted iff CI upper bound `<= t`.
- Equivalence claim (`|delta| <= epsilon`): accepted iff CI for `delta` is fully contained in `[-epsilon, +epsilon]`.
```

## ⚠️ Not ready to approve The new normative protocol spec contains ambiguities (e.g., CI sidedness and an undefined “very small n” cutoff) that could lead to inconsistent or conflicting implementations of gating decisions.
Pull request overview This PR formalizes decision D2 by defining normative reproducibility semantics (byte reproducible vs behaviorally equivalent) and establishing a confidence-bounded protocol for empirical claims (Gate K), then wiring those definitions into the R4G1 RFC and the implementation plan. **Changes:** - Adds a new normative specification document for BR/BE and Gate K empirical-claim acceptance rules. - Updates `R4G1.md` §7 to reference the new spec and remove “working assumption” language. - Updates the implementation plan backlog item to link directly to the new spec.
File summaries | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | docs/transformerless/R4G1.md | Replaces the prior D2 “working assumption” text with a normative reference to the new BR/BE + Gate K protocol spec. | | docs/transformerless/EQUIVALENCE_AND_EMPIRICAL_PROTOCOL.md | Introduces the normative BR/BE definitions and a confidence-bounded empirical-claims protocol with acceptance rules. | | docs/r4_graph_compiler_implementation_plan.md | Links plan item 23 directly to the new normative spec document. | ### Review details - **Files reviewed:** 3/3 changed files - **Comments generated:** 2 - **Review effort level:** Low

review_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,88 @@
+# Behavioral Equivalence and Empirical-Claims Protocol (Issue #33)
+
+Status: normative Phase-0/3 specification for plan §9 item 23; feeds decision D2.
+
+This document defines:
+
+1. **Byte reproducibility** for certificate-bearing artifacts.
+2. **Behavioral graph equivalence** (PDF §15) for non-canonical compile modes.
+3. The **confidence-bounded statistical protocol** required for *all empirical claims*.
+
+## 1. Reproducibility classes (D2)
+
+### Class BR — byte reproducible
+
+An artifact is **byte reproducible** iff two independent compiles with identical pinned inputs:
+
+- source model CID + revision,
+- tokenizer CID,
+- corpus CIDs and split declaration (D3),
+- compiler version and canonical deterministic mode,
+- seed set and declared compile options,
+
+produce byte-identical artifact and certificate payloads (equivalently, identical CIDs).
+
+Class BR is mandatory for certificate-bearing artifacts used to satisfy Gate E.
+
+### Class BE — behaviorally equivalent
+
+Two artifacts are **behaviorally equivalent** when BR is not expected (for example, platform FP/SIMD
+local-iteration compiles), but both satisfy the same declared behavioral contract on the same
+evaluation distribution:
+
+- identical runtime semantics and fallback policy class,
+- identical declared metric set and acceptance thresholds,
+- pairwise metric deltas within predeclared equivalence margins (PDF §15 framing),
+- confidence bounds that stay within those margins per §2.
+
+BE supports local iteration and cross-platform comparison, but does not replace BR for
+certificate-bearing release artifacts.
+
+## 2. Confidence-bounded empirical-claims protocol (Gate K)
+
+Every empirical claim MUST ship a claim record containing:
+
+- distribution identifier and corpus CIDs (D3),
+- unit of analysis and sample size `n`,
+- metric definition and direction (higher/lower is better),
+- estimator, uncertainty method, and confidence level,
+- acceptance threshold (or equivalence margin),
+- random seeds, stopping rule, and slice definitions.
+
+### 2.1 Required estimators and intervals
+
+- **Rates/proportions** (agreement, recall, abstention): Wilson interval (or exact binomial for very
+  small `n`).
review_comments.body: The phrase “very small n” is undefined in this normative spec, which makes the allowed interval method for rates/proportions ambiguous and hard to implement consistently. Consider allowing either Wilson or exact (Clopper–Pearson) binomial intervals unconditionally, with the chosen method recorded in the claim record.

+
+Default confidence level is 95% (`alpha = 0.05`) unless a stricter level is declared in advance.
review_comments.body: The spec doesn’t define whether “CI” is one-sided or two-sided. Because the acceptance rules for lower/upper-bounded and non-inferiority claims only check one bound, implementers could reasonably use either a two-sided 95% CI or a one-sided 95% CI, which changes gating outcomes. Please explicitly specify sidedness for intervals used in §2.2.
